Starting with a dense, decreasing sequence {Pn}, the proof derives a contradiction assuming the limit of |Pn| is positive. This contradiction arises because any such limit would imply the existence of atoms—violating the non-atomicity assumption. The construction of nested sets Fn ensures that μ(F) remains bounded away from zero, leading to a contradiction when attempting to approximate any set within arbitrary precision using unions of partition elements. The key insight is that in a non-atomic setting, arbitrarily fine partitions must exist, forcing |Pn| → 0. This convergence underpins both the approximation property (measure distance) and the recursive structure (nested partitions).
